key_insight: Neutral-atom quantum graph features capture structural signatures complementary to classical descriptors, with clear gains on a specific ladder-graph classification task.
engineering_relevance: Hardware-derived quantum features can augment conventional graph-learning models, though most reported downstream gains remain within cross-fold noise.
method: Probe graph-dependent Rydberg Hamiltonians through dynamical correlation measurements.
Tune quench parameters to access antiferromagnetic-like and ferromagnetic-like correlation regimes.
Combine quantum and classical features in message-passing, attention, and graph-transformer models.
evidence_signal: Evaluation covers 15 topological and spectral probes; compressed QPU-derived hybrid features match emulated counterparts within 0.01 F1 across all tested backbones, while ladder-graph gains exceed cross-fold variability.
watch_item: Broad practical advantage remains unproven: most downstream improvements are within cross-fold noise, and the clearest separation is on two specific synthetic ladder-graph classes.
paper_title: Neutral-atom quantum features as complementary structural encodings for graph learning
